correctness.rationale: The four-dimensional map yields the exact cubic-delay equation for n>=2. A small open positive region remains in the positive-memristance zone; its bounded logarithmic forcing has a positive rho-Perron component. At the endpoint an order-preserving self-map of a compact product interval has a positive fixed sequence realized by explicit positive four-dimensional initial data. The tail is asymptotic to its first term, changing the logarithmic companion polynomial from t^3-t^2-2 to t^3-2t^2-2. Its non-Perron eigenvalues have modulus sqrt(2/beta)<1; the limiting constant particular solution produces the universal prefactor. Symbolic reduction and finite direct map tests pass, but tests are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The memory coordinate has a natural critical surface w=sqrt(2) where the published quadratic memristance vanishes. The finding proves that a nonempty family of positive orbits actually approaches this surface, with a qualitatively faster double-exponential exponent beta>rho and exact first prefactor; nearby interior-memory positive orbits have rho instead. This is a motivated dynamical transition and a quantitative nonlinear stability result not provided by linearization, mere parameter substitution, or the known 3D rho law.
